::: {.hero-lede}
Learning has always been mediated by and distributed across people and their
environment. Assessment, however, asks us to say something about *people*. My
work is about how we bridge that gap — how activity that is shared with others
and with tools can still license a defensible claim about an individual.
:::

## What I work on

A final product conceals the process that produced it. When a person works with
a tool, that product may no longer support a claim about what *they* know or can
do. Generative AI did not create this problem, but it has made it impossible to
ignore.

I treat the assessment of AI-assisted activity as a problem of **measurement
rather than integrity**. What we want to measure is learning. What we have to
account for is *interdependence* — the structure that arises as people and tools
respond to and build on one another's contributions. Accounting for it is what
allows evidence of joint activity to say something about individuals.

That commitment runs through a chain of inference, and my work contributes a
method and an instrument at each link:

:::: {.chain}
::: {.chain-step}
[01]{.n}[Observe]{.t}[The *Trace* platform captures writing activity across the tools people actually use.]{.d}
:::
::: {.chain-step}
[02]{.n}[Code]{.t}[Theory-driven LLM classifiers, with validation procedures built for stochastic coders.]{.d}
:::
::: {.chain-step}
[03]{.n}[Model]{.t}[Epistemic and ordered network analysis, extended with graph neural networks.]{.d}
:::
::: {.chain-step}
[04]{.n}[Claim]{.t}[What distinguishes stronger work is not *that* people use AI but *how* they question it.]{.d}
:::
::: {.chain-step}
[05]{.n}[Represent]{.t}[*Trace: Replay* renders a writing session so learners and educators can read it.]{.d}
:::
::::

## Currently

- Leading two Australian Research Council projects as Primary Chief Investigator
  (PI equivalent) — an **ARC DECRA** on authentic assessment for the age of
  generative AI, and an **ARC Discovery Project**, with a multi-institutional
  team, on assessments for writing with generative AI.
- Taking the browser-extension version of *Trace* out of closed beta and into
  in-the-wild studies of writing.
- Building and validating LLM-based classifiers for AI-assisted writing —
  structured code refinement, hold-out testing against human coders, and
  stability testing across repeated classification.
- Supervising doctoral students working on discourse classification, simulation
  of collaborative discourse, and the ethics of trace data in AI-assisted
  writing.

## Background

I completed my PhD in Educational Psychology at the University of
Wisconsin–Madison in 2020, working in the Epistemic Analytics Lab, after a BS in
Physics and Mathematics at the University of Alabama. I have been at Monash
since 2020, a Senior Lecturer since 2024, and hold an ARC Discovery Early Career
Researcher Award from 2026 to 2029.

I serve on the editorial boards of the *International Journal of
Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning* and the *Journal of Quantitative
Ethnography*, was program co-chair of ICQE24, and co-chair the Poster and Demo
track for LAK26.
